questions.q: Why does LTV Global's data model use a Person Account for end customers but a standard Business Account for dealers?
options: Because end customers are individuals who directly own equipment, while dealers are businesses with their own internal structure and hierarchy
Because Person Accounts are required for any object with more than a million records
Because Business Accounts cannot be used by any custom object
Because Person Accounts are only available in Experience Cloud
questions.explain: Person Accounts fit LTV Global's millions of individual equipment-owning end customers, while dealers, as businesses with multi-location hierarchies, fit the standard Business Account model.

questions.q: Why does this lesson choose a custom Equipment Asset object instead of the standard Asset object?
options: Because Salesforce does not allow the standard Asset object to be used by custom automation
Because the standard Asset object cannot have a lookup to Account
Because Equipment Asset needs fields and automation specific to heavy industrial equipment that would require heavily customizing the standard object anyway, losing its main out-of-box benefit
Because custom objects are always preferred over standard objects in enterprise designs
questions.explain: The lesson's reasoning is specific: the needed customization (serial number formatting, warranty/Service Contract linkage, dealer lookup) would be so extensive that the standard object's main benefit — out-of-box behavior — would be lost anyway.

questions.q: Why is the Service Contract to Equipment Asset relationship master-detail, while Parts Order to Equipment Asset is a lookup?
options: Master-detail and lookup are interchangeable, and the choice here is arbitrary

Because a Service Contract is meaningless without its specific equipment and should inherit its sharing, while Parts Order is high-volume and would inherit costly sharing-recalculation behavior under master-detail
Because Parts Order is a standard object and cannot use master-detail
Because master-detail relationships are forbidden on any object related to a Person Account
questions.explain: The relationship type is chosen deliberately based on each object's actual volume and sharing needs: Service Contract benefits from inheriting Equipment Asset's sharing, while Parts Order's high volume makes that same inheritance a performance risk.

questions.q: What does Case relate to in LTV Global's data model, per this lesson's object table?
options: Only to Opportunity, with no link to equipment at all
No relationship at all — Case stands alone in this design
A master-detail relationship to Account directly
A lookup to Equipment Asset and a lookup to Service Contract
questions.explain: The object table shows Case with a lookup to Equipment Asset and a lookup to Service Contract, supporting the standard Field Service case model this design replaces EuroCRM's functionality with.

questions.q: What does this lesson say about the Parts Order object's relationship type choice, specifically regarding sharing recalculation?
options: A lookup relationship was chosen so Parts Order does not inherit Equipment Asset's OWD and sharing recalculation behavior at high volume
Master-detail was chosen specifically to maximize sharing recalculation at scale
Parts Order has no relationship to Equipment Asset of any kind
Sharing recalculation is not a consideration for any object in this data model
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly ties the lookup choice for Parts Order to avoiding costly sharing-recalculation inheritance at the object's high transaction volume, a concern Lesson 10 develops further.
